title: Dabuyid Dynasty
capsule: The Dabuyids were a Zoroastrian Iranian dynasty that held the Caspian province of Tabaristan (modern Mazandaran) as a semi-autonomous principality from the mid-7th century onward, resisting Arab Muslim conquest longer than almost any other Iranian ruling house. Their founder Gil Gavbara (Dabuyeh) established control around 642 after the fall of the Sasanian Empire, and the dynasty perpetuated Sasanian administrative and religious traditions in a forested mountain redoubt that frustrated repeated Umayyad campaigns. The dynasty's most prominent ruler, Farrukhan the Great (r. c. 712–728), repelled Arab incursions and left inscriptions in Middle Persian. The last Dabuyid, Khurshid, was driven out by Abbasid forces under the Mawali general Rawwad ibn Muthanna around 760, after which he fled east and was killed, ending the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Dabuyid sequence and terminal dates are reasonably attested through Arabic chronicles and Middle Persian inscriptions from Tabaristan, but precise reign dates for individual rulers remain disputed by a decade or more.
